title: Four US trawl samples gave uncertain contrasts between same-year and next-year sea temperature links in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested whether annual catch-latitude changes had a stronger link to same-year sea surface temperature changes than to next-year changes. We used fixed strata, area weights and persistent taxa in Bering Sea and Northeast US fall surveys in 1982-1999 and 2000-2019. Four joint first-difference models gave positive coefficient contrasts of 5.99 to 9.05 km per C. All four adjusted bootstrap intervals included zero. A short temperature window gave a positive late Bering Sea interval, but this did not repeat across all samples. These results do not establish a common timing difference or equal effects. Short records, surface temperature, selected taxa, catchability and residual sampling bias limit inference. We do not test pollution or attribute changes to human-driven warming. The package gives code, source hashes, derived evidence and offline checks.

display.caption: Same-year minus next-year temperature-change coefficients for annual latitude displacement. Intervals are 98.75% residual-block bootstrap intervals for four planned comparisons. All include zero.
